source_refs.note: Practice MCQs written from Chapter 25 (PDF 134-144, printed 131-141); not printed in the book. Based on the chapter's text, tables, boxes and worked examples (numericals with changed values); none repeats the chapter exercise. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 25 (Organic Synthesis), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.

blocks.prompt: 1 The study of organic chemistry is organized around:
blocks.explanation: The study of organic chemistry is organized around functional groups; each one defines a family of organic compounds (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: The study of organic chemistry is organized around functional groups.

blocks.prompt: 2 A functional group is that part of an organic compound where:

options.text: only the carbon skeleton is present

blocks.explanation: A functional group is the part of an organic compound where most of the reactions occur (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: Functional group is a part of organic compound where most of the reactions occur.

blocks.prompt: 3 Millions of organic compounds are known. The number of functional groups is:

options.text: only a handful, each defining a family of compounds
equal to the number of compounds
only one, common to all compounds

blocks.explanation: Although millions of organic compounds are known, there are only a handful of functional groups and each one defines a family of organic compounds (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: there are only a handful of functional groups and each one serves to define a family

blocks.prompt: 4 In designing a synthesis, functional groups enable chemists to:

options.text: change the atomic number of carbon
predict and control the reactions leading to the desired product

blocks.explanation: Functional groups play a central role in designing a synthesis; they enable chemists to predict and control the reactions that lead to the desired product (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: They enable chemists to predict and control the reactions which ultimately lead to the desired product.

blocks.prompt: 5 Identifying the functional group present in a compound mainly helps to:

options.text: find the colour of its flame
predict the properties of the compound

blocks.explanation: Identifying a functional group can help to predict the properties of the compound; this is crucial for new products and for checking the purity of medicines and food additives (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: Identifying a functional group present in a compound can help to predict the properties of the compound.

blocks.prompt: 6 Knowledge of functional groups helps to ensure the purity and composition of products such as:
blocks.explanation: The book names medicines and food additives as products whose purity and composition are ensured with the help of functional group information (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: as well as to ensure the purity and composition of the products such as medicines and food additives.

blocks.prompt: 7 Which of the following is a feature of a good synthesis?

options.text: costly starting materials and many steps
the largest possible number of steps
cheap starting materials, least number of steps and high overall yield
low overall yield with rare reagents

blocks.explanation: A good synthesis converts cheap and easily available starting materials to the product by a route with the least number of steps and a high overall yield (25.1).

book_ref.quote: A good synthesis of a substance involves the conversion of cheap and easily available starting materials

blocks.prompt: 8 Most organic compounds can be prepared by:

options.text: a number of different routes, so criteria are needed to select the best

blocks.explanation: Most organic compounds can be prepared by a number of different routes, and criteria are required to select the best route (25.1).

book_ref.quote: Most organic compounds can be prepared by a number of different routes

blocks.prompt: 9 Organic reactions used in synthesis are categorized according to whether they bring about:

options.text: functional group interconversion or carbon-carbon bond formation

blocks.explanation: Reactions useful in synthesis are categorized by whether they bring about functional group interconversions (FGI) or carbon-carbon bond formation (25.1).

book_ref.quote: They can be categorized as whether they bring about functional group interconversions (FGI) or a carbon-carbon bond formation.

blocks.prompt: 10 Carbon-carbon bond formation reactions are particularly important in synthesis because:

options.text: the target molecule is assembled from simple and smaller starting materials

blocks.explanation: The basic strategy of synthesis is to assemble the target molecule from simple and smaller starting materials, so C–C bond formation is particularly important (25.1).

book_ref.quote: Carbon-carbon bond formation reactions are particularly important because the basic strategy

blocks.prompt: 11 In synthesis, the target molecule is prepared starting from:
blocks.explanation: In synthesis the target molecule is prepared from simple commercially available compounds, in one or many steps (25.1.1).

book_ref.quote: In synthesis, the target molecule is prepared starting from simple commercially available compounds.

blocks.prompt: 12 A primary aliphatic amine can be prepared in a single step by treating ammonia with:
blocks.explanation: A primary aliphatic amine is prepared in a single step by treating a haloalkane with ammonia: R–CH₂–Cl + NH₃ → R–CH₂–NH₂ + HCl (25.1.1).

book_ref.quote: primary aliphatic amine can be prepared in a single step by treating a haloalkane with ammonia.

blocks.prompt: 13 In the one-step synthesis of a primary aliphatic amine (25.1.1), the haloalkane is treated with:
blocks.explanation: Primary aliphatic amine can be prepared in a single step by treating a haloalkane with ammonia: R–CH₂–Cl + NH₃ → R–CH₂–NH₂ + HCl (25.1.1).

book_ref.quote: primary aliphatic amine can be prepared in a single step by treating a haloalkane with ammonia

blocks.prompt: 14 In the two-step synthesis of an alkyl amine, the starting material is an alcohol because:

options.text: the haloalkane is not easily available, while the alcohol is more easily available
alcohols cannot be converted to haloalkanes
amines are made only from alkanes
alcohols react directly with ammonia to give amides

blocks.explanation: Haloalkane is not easily available, so it is prepared from an alcohol, which is more easily available; the synthesis is then completed in two steps (25.1.1).

book_ref.quote: Since haloalkane is not easily available rather it is prepared from an alcohol

blocks.prompt: 15 In the conversion R–CH₂–OH → R–CH₂–Cl → R–CH₂–NH₂, the reagent used for the first step is:
blocks.explanation: The alcohol is first converted to the chloroalkane with SOCl₂, and the chloroalkane then gives the amine with NH₃ (25.1.1).

book_ref.quote: The synthesis of an alkyl amine may be completed in two steps.

blocks.prompt: 16 Retrosynthesis is best described as:

options.text: the same as synthesis, started from cheap compounds
measuring the yield of a reaction
exactly the opposite of synthesis, working back from the target molecule

blocks.explanation: Retrosynthesis is exactly the opposite of synthesis: the target molecule is broken down into simpler, readily available compounds that serve as starting materials (25.1.2).

book_ref.quote: It is exactly the opposite of the synthesis.

blocks.prompt: 17 Retrosynthesis involves the:
blocks.explanation: Retrosynthesis involves the disconnection approach, in which bonds of the target molecule are broken in imagination (25.1.2).

book_ref.quote: Retrosynthesis involves the disconnection approach.

blocks.prompt: 18 In retrosynthesis, which bonds of the target molecule are disconnected?

options.text: those that give a considerable structural simplification

blocks.explanation: Those bonds are disconnected that result in a considerable structural simplification; after a series of disconnections simple, easily available starting materials are reached (25.1.2).

book_ref.quote: those bonds of the target molecule are disconnected that result in a considerable structural simplification

blocks.prompt: 19 In retrosynthesis, the abbreviation TM stands for:
blocks.explanation: Target Molecule (TM) is the molecule which is to be prepared (25.1, terminology).

book_ref.quote: Target Molecule (TM) is the molecule which is to be prepared by disconnection.

blocks.prompt: 20 In disconnection, the breaking of the target molecule into simpler starting materials is:

options.text: a real reaction done with heat

blocks.explanation: Disconnection involves the imaginary breaking down of the TM progressively into simpler starting materials (25.1, terminology).

book_ref.quote: Disconnection is a process which involves the imaginary breaking down of the TM

blocks.prompt: 21 Synthons generated by a disconnection are often:

options.text: stable neutral reagents sold in bottles
ionic species that act as building blocks

blocks.explanation: Synthons are fragments of the target molecule produced by disconnection; they are often ionic species and represent the building blocks for the synthesis (25.1, terminology).

book_ref.quote: They are often an ionic species and represent the building blocks for the synthesis.

blocks.prompt: 22 A synthetic equivalent (SE) is used in place of a synthon because the synthon:

options.text: is usually unstable and cannot be used itself

blocks.explanation: A synthetic equivalent is a reagent that carries out the function of a synthon, which cannot itself be used because it is usually unstable (25.1, terminology).

book_ref.quote: Synthetic Equivalent (SE) is a reagent used to carry out the function of a synthon

blocks.prompt: 23 A diagram showing all possible disconnections and synthons from the target molecule to the starting materials is called:
blocks.explanation: A retrosynthetic tree is a diagram showing all possible disconnections and synthons from the target molecule to the starting materials (25.1, terminology).

book_ref.quote: Retrosynthetic Tree is a diagram showing all possible disconnections and synthons

blocks.prompt: 24 FGI has a crucial role in:

options.text: designing routes that lead to target molecules

blocks.explanation: FGI has a crucial role to play in designing routes which lead to target molecules (FGI).

book_ref.quote: FGI has a crucial role to play in designing routes which lead to target molecules.

blocks.prompt: 25 According to the chapter, FGI allows a chemist to:

options.text: create the carbon skeleton of the TM and also select the route

blocks.explanation: FGI not only allows the carbon skeleton of the target molecule to be created but also helps select the route to be adopted (FGI).

book_ref.quote: FGI not only allows to create the carbon skeleton of the target molecule but also select the route

blocks.prompt: 26 In Figure 25.3, which reagent converts the alcohol CH₃-CH₂-OH into the halogenoalkane CH₃-CH₂-Br?
blocks.explanation: In Figure 25.3 the alcohol is converted into the halogenoalkane with PBr₃; KOH (aq) does the reverse, halogenoalkane to alcohol (FGI).

book_ref.quote: a summary of these interconversions is given in Figure 25.3 and 25.4

blocks.text: 25.2 Retrosynthesis and Synthesis of Some Compounds

blocks.prompt: 27 Retrosynthesis of ethyl acetate (TM) gives which simpler starting materials?
blocks.explanation: For ethyl acetate the disconnection followed by neutralization gives acetic acid and ethanol; the printed 'benzene and nitric acid' belongs to the aniline example (25.2, book correction).

book_ref.quote: For our target molecule ethyl acetate, the disconnection followed by neutralization yields acetic acid and ethanol

blocks.prompt: 28 In the retrosynthesis of ethyl acetate, synthon B is C₂H₅O⁻. Its synthetic equivalent is:
blocks.explanation: Synthon A (CH₃CO⁺) has acetic acid as its SE and synthon B (C₂H₅O⁻) has ethanol as its SE (25.2, book correction).

book_ref.quote: For ethyl acetate the synthetic equivalents are acetic acid (for synthon A, CH₃CO⁺)

blocks.prompt: 29 While selecting synthetic equivalents, the essential condition is that they:

options.text: should not react with each other
should be heavier than the TM
should react together to give the target molecule

blocks.explanation: Synthetic equivalents should undergo reaction to give the target molecule; otherwise the disconnection is of no use (25.2).

book_ref.quote: While selecting synthetic equivalent molecules thus obtained, they should undergo reaction to give the target molecule.

blocks.prompt: 30 Ethyl acetate is synthesized from acetic acid and ethanol by:

options.text: esterification in the presence of H₂SO₄

blocks.explanation: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH → (H₂SO₄) CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O, a very familiar esterification reaction (25.2).

book_ref.quote: Here we can design the synthesis of our TM by a very familiar esterification reaction

blocks.prompt: 31 In the esterification CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH → CH₃COOC₂H₅ + X, the by-product X is:
blocks.explanation: The esterification of acetic acid with ethanol gives ethyl acetate and water (25.2).

book_ref.quote: Disconnection at the position indicated will enable us to get synthon A and synthon B

blocks.prompt: 32 In the retrosynthesis of aniline, the first step is:

options.text: FGI of the –NH₂ group into the –NO₂ group

blocks.explanation: The first step of the retrosynthesis of aniline is FGI, in which the amino group (–NH₂) is converted into the nitro group (–NO₂) (25.2.2).

book_ref.quote: First step of retrosynthesis here is FGI, where amino group (NH₂) is converted into nitro (NO₂) group.

blocks.prompt: 33 FGI of –NH₂ to –NO₂ is done in the retrosynthesis of aniline because:

options.text: an amino group cannot exist on benzene
a nitro group is easily attached to benzene by electrophilic substitution, unlike an amino group by nucleophilic substitution
a nitro group is removed by esterification

blocks.explanation: It is easy to attach a nitro group on benzene by electrophilic substitution, rather than an amino group by nucleophilic substitution (25.2.2).

book_ref.quote: Because it is easy to attach nitro group on benzene by electrophilic substitution

blocks.prompt: 34 Disconnection of nitrobenzene at the C–N bond gives the synthons:
blocks.explanation: The C–N disconnection of nitrobenzene creates the aryl anion C₆H₅⁻ and the nitronium cation NO₂⁺ (25.2.2).

book_ref.quote: the disconnection of nitrobenzene was done from C—N bond, which created synthons of aryl anion

blocks.prompt: 35 The synthetic equivalents of the synthons C₆H₅⁻ and NO₂⁺ in the aniline example are:
blocks.explanation: Neutralizing the synthons gives benzene (for C₆H₅⁻) and nitric acid (for NO₂⁺) as synthetic equivalents (25.2.2).

book_ref.quote: These synthons were neutralized to get synthetic equivalents i.e., benzene and nitric acid molecule.

blocks.prompt: 36 How many steps (FGI, disconnection, synthetic equivalents) are shown in the retrosynthetic tree of aniline in the chapter?
blocks.explanation: The aniline tree has Step I FGI, Step II disconnection and Step III synthetic equivalents: three steps (25.2.2).

book_ref.quote: First step of retrosynthesis here is FGI

blocks.prompt: 37 In the retrosynthesis of acetophenone, the first disconnection is made at the:

options.text: C–H bond of the methyl group
C–C bond between the ring and the acyl group

blocks.explanation: The disconnection of acetophenone is done at the C–C bond, creating the aryl anion C₆H₅⁻ and the acylium cation CH₃CO⁺ (25.2.3).

book_ref.quote: In first step the disconnection of acetophenone (TM) was done from C—C bond

blocks.prompt: 38 The cationic synthon obtained from acetophenone is called:
blocks.explanation: Disconnection of acetophenone gives the aryl anion C₆H₅⁻ and the acylium cation CH₃CO⁺ (25.2.3).

book_ref.quote: which created synthons of aryl anion (C₆H₅⁻) and acylium (CH₃CO⁺) cation.

blocks.prompt: 39 The synthetic equivalents used to make acetophenone are:
blocks.explanation: Neutralizing C₆H₅⁻ and CH₃CO⁺ gives benzene and acyl chloride, CH₃COCl (25.2.3).

book_ref.quote: These synthons were neutralized to get synthetic equivalents i.e., benzene and acyl chloride molecule.

blocks.prompt: 40 The catalyst used in the Friedel-Craft acylation of benzene to acetophenone is:
blocks.explanation: Benzene reacts with acyl chloride in the presence of AlCl₃ as catalyst (Friedel-Craft acylation): C₆H₆ + CH₃COCl → C₆H₅COCH₃ + HCl (25.2.3).

book_ref.quote: in the presence of AlCl₃ as catalyst, using Friedel-Craft acylation process.

blocks.prompt: 41 In C₆H₆ + CH₃COCl → (AlCl₃) C₆H₅COCH₃ + Y, the by-product Y is:
blocks.explanation: The Friedel-Craft acylation of benzene with acyl chloride gives acetophenone and HCl (25.2.3).

book_ref.quote: Synthesis of acetophenone can be done by reaction between benzene and acyl chloride

blocks.prompt: 42 The landmark synthesis of cholesterol was first achieved in the early 1950s by groups headed by:
blocks.explanation: Cholesterol was first synthesized in the early 1950s by two competing groups headed by Robert Robinson in Oxford and R.B. Woodward at Harvard (Interesting Information).

book_ref.quote: The landmark synthesis of cholesterol was first achieved in early 1950s

blocks.prompt: 43 In the retrosynthesis of phenyl ethanoate (Quick Check 25.2), the synthetic equivalents are:
blocks.explanation: Disconnecting the C–O bond of the ester gives CH₃CO⁺ and C₆H₅O⁻; their synthetic equivalents are ethanoyl chloride and phenol (Quick Check 25.2).

book_ref.quote: Synthetic equivalents: ethanoyl chloride (CH₃COCl) for CH₃CO⁺, and phenol (C₆H₅OH) for C₆H₅O⁻.

blocks.prompt: 44 One of the most important applications of retrosynthesis is in the synthesis of:
blocks.explanation: One of the most important applications of retrosynthesis is in pharmaceutical product synthesis (25.3).

book_ref.quote: One of the most important applications of retrosynthesis is in pharmaceutical product synthesis.

blocks.prompt: 45 Complex medicinal compounds can be traced back to simple, commonly available starting materials if they are:
blocks.explanation: Medicinal compounds look very complex, but if they are disconnected properly and efficiently we can approach very simple and commonly available starting materials (25.3).

book_ref.quote: if they are disconnected properly and efficiently, we can approach to very simple and commonly available starting materials

blocks.prompt: 46 The first disconnection of paracetamol is made at the:

options.text: C–O bond of the hydroxy group
C–N bond of the amide group

blocks.explanation: The first step of the retrosynthesis of paracetamol is the disconnection of the C–N bond in the amide group (25.3.1).

book_ref.quote: The first step is the disconnection of paracetamol from C—N bond in amide group to get synthons.

blocks.prompt: 47 After the first disconnection of paracetamol, the synthetic equivalents are:
blocks.explanation: Step II of the paracetamol retrosynthesis gives 4-aminophenol and acyl chloride as synthetic equivalents (25.3.1).

book_ref.quote: These synthons were neutralized to get synthetic equivalents i.e., 4-aminophenol and acyl chloride molecule.

blocks.prompt: 48 4-Aminophenol and acyl chloride react to form the amide bond of paracetamol through:
blocks.explanation: The bond is broken at that position because its synthetic equivalents are well known to react through a nucleophilic addition-elimination reaction (25.3.1).

book_ref.quote: are well known to react through a nucleophilic addition-elimination reaction.

blocks.prompt: 49 In the retrosynthesis of paracetamol, FGI converts 4-aminophenol into 4-nitrophenol because:

options.text: a nitro group is the final drug
p-nitrophenol is easy to prepare and can be reduced to p-aminophenol
p-nitrophenol reacts with acyl chloride to give paracetamol

blocks.explanation: FGI is done because p-nitrophenol is easy to prepare and can then be reduced to p-aminophenol (25.3.1).

book_ref.quote: FGI has been done because it is easy to prepare p-nitrophenol and it can then be reduced to p-aminophenol.

blocks.prompt: 50 In Step IV of the retrosynthesis of paracetamol, the C–N disconnection of 4-nitrophenol gives which synthons?
blocks.explanation: Step IV disconnects 4-nitrophenol; the 4-hydroxy aryl anion is HO–C₆H₄⁻ (not C₆H₅⁻ as printed) and the other synthon is the nitronium cation NO₂⁺ (25.3.1, book correction).

book_ref.quote: Step IV disconnects 4-nitrophenol (the molecule drawn in the scheme), not 4-aminophenol.

blocks.prompt: 51 In Step V of the retrosynthesis of paracetamol, the synthetic equivalents are:
blocks.explanation: The synthetic equivalents in Step V are phenol (for HO–C₆H₄⁻) and nitric acid (for NO₂⁺); the printed 'benzene' is a misprint (25.3.1, book correction).

book_ref.quote: The synthetic equivalents in Step V are phenol (for the 4-hydroxy aryl anion) and nitric acid

blocks.prompt: 52 In the retrosynthesis of paracetamol, Step III (FGI) changes 4-aminophenol into:
blocks.explanation: FGI has been done because it is easy to prepare p-nitrophenol and it can then be reduced to p-aminophenol (25.3.1, Step III).

book_ref.quote: FGI has been done because it is easy to prepare p-nitrophenol

blocks.prompt: 53 The direct synthesis of paracetamol requires:

options.text: a series of steps, decoded by its retrosynthesis

blocks.explanation: Direct synthesis of paracetamol requires a series of steps, and this series is decoded by its retrosynthesis (25.3.1).

book_ref.quote: It can be seen that direct synthesis of paracetamol requires a series of steps.

blocks.prompt: 54 The first disconnection of aspirin is made at the:

options.text: C–O bond of the ester linkage
C–N bond of the amide group
C–C bond of the carboxylic group

blocks.explanation: The first step of the retrosynthesis of aspirin is the disconnection of the C–O bond in the ester linkage (25.3.2).

book_ref.quote: The first step is the disconnection of Aspirin from C—O bond in ester linkage to get synthons.

blocks.prompt: 55 After the first disconnection of aspirin, the synthetic equivalents obtained are:
blocks.explanation: Step II of the aspirin retrosynthesis gives salicylic acid and acetic anhydride (25.3.2).

book_ref.quote: These synthons were neutralized to get synthetic equivalents i.e., salicylic acid and acetic anhydride molecule.

blocks.prompt: 56 The second disconnection in the retrosynthesis of aspirin breaks the:

options.text: C–C bond of the carboxylic group

blocks.explanation: Disconnection-II breaks the C–C bond of the carboxylic group of salicylic acid (25.3.2).

book_ref.quote: Next disconnection is the C—C bond of carboxylic group.

blocks.prompt: 57 The synthetic equivalents obtained from the second disconnection of aspirin are:
blocks.explanation: Step IV of the aspirin retrosynthesis gives phenol and carbon dioxide (25.3.2).

book_ref.quote: These synthons were neutralized to get synthetic equivalents i.e., phenol and carbon dioxide molecule.

blocks.prompt: 58 The common simple starting material for both aspirin and paracetamol is:
blocks.explanation: Both aspirin and paracetamol are synthesized starting from phenol (Quick Check 25.3).

book_ref.quote: Aspirin and Paracetamol, both are synthesized starting from phenol.

blocks.prompt: 59 Using retrosynthesis on aspirin helps to find:

options.text: how many and which steps are needed to prepare it from phenol

blocks.explanation: By retrosynthesis we can find how many and which steps are actually needed to prepare aspirin from phenol, the simple starting material (25.3.2).

book_ref.quote: By retrosynthesis we can truly find how many and which steps are actually needed to prepare Aspirin from phenol

blocks.text: 25.4 Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Drug Designing

blocks.prompt: 60 The current methods of developing new drugs are described in the chapter as:

options.text: very costly, time consuming and limited to a narrow spectrum of chemical activity

blocks.explanation: Current drug-development methods are very costly, time consuming and usually limited to a narrow spectrum of chemical activity (25.4).

book_ref.quote: The methods which are currently used to develop new drugs are very costly, time consuming

blocks.prompt: 61 The growing problem mentioned in 25.4 is that:

options.text: pathogens (bacteria) become resistant to the prevalent antibiotics

blocks.explanation: Pathogens (bacteria) become resistant to the prevalent antibiotics; the printed sentence is reversed (25.4, book correction).

book_ref.quote: the pathogens (bacteria) become resistant to the prevalent antibiotics.

blocks.prompt: 62 The machine-learning algorithm designed at MIT looked for chemical features that make molecules effective at killing:
blocks.explanation: Researchers at MIT designed a machine-learning algorithm to look for chemical features that make molecules effective at killing E. coli bacteria (25.4).

book_ref.quote: designed a machine-learning algorithm to look for chemical features that make molecules effective at killing E. coli bacteria

blocks.prompt: 63 According to the chapter, the MIT model was first applied on:

options.text: 2500 molecules and a set of 800 natural products

blocks.explanation: The model was applied on 2500 molecules and a set of 800 natural products with different structures and a wide range of bioactivities (25.4).

book_ref.quote: they applied the model on 2500 molecules and a set of 800 natural products

blocks.prompt: 64 Compared with the existing antibiotics, the molecular structure of the molecule picked out by the computer model (later named halicin) was:

options.text: only slightly different, like recent antibiotics
the same as one of the 800 natural products

blocks.explanation: The model picked out one molecule predicted to have antibacterial properties with a molecular structure different from the existing antibiotics (25.4).

book_ref.quote: with a molecular structure different from the existing antibiotics.

blocks.prompt: 65 Using a different model, the researchers showed that halicin would most likely show:
blocks.explanation: A different model showed that the molecule would most likely show low toxicity to human cells (25.4).

book_ref.quote: this molecule would most likely show low toxicity to human cells.

blocks.prompt: 66 When tested against bacterial strains isolated from patients, halicin:

options.text: killed many problematic bacteria that were previously resistant to treatment

blocks.explanation: Halicin killed many of the world's most problematic disease-causing bacteria which were previously resistant to treatment (25.4).

book_ref.quote: the new molecule killed many of the world's most problematic disease-causing bacteria

blocks.prompt: 67 In the structure of halicin, the top atom of both five-membered rings is:
blocks.explanation: In halicin the top atom of both five-membered rings is sulfur; the printed structure leaves it unlabelled, which wrongly implies carbon (25.4, book correction).

book_ref.quote: in halicin it is sulfur in both rings

blocks.prompt: 68 After identifying halicin, the computer model screened more than 100 million molecules in:
blocks.explanation: The screening of more than 100 million molecules from a database was completed in only three days (25.4).

book_ref.quote: the researchers applied their computer model to screen more than 100 million molecules

blocks.prompt: 69 Of the 23 further molecules selected by the screening, how many showed antibacterial activity, and how many were particularly powerful?

options.text: all 23 showed activity; eight were powerful
two showed activity; one was powerful
eight showed activity; two were particularly powerful

blocks.explanation: The screening selected 23 more molecules; eight showed antibacterial activities and two were particularly powerful (25.4).

book_ref.quote: Researchers further, found that eight of these molecules showed antibacterial activities

blocks.prompt: 70 The historic total synthesis of vitamin B₁₂ (1972) was achieved by:

options.text: researchers at MIT using machine learning

blocks.explanation: The total synthesis of vitamin B₁₂ was achieved by R.B. Woodward and A. Eschenmoser in 1972 after over 10 years of collaboration (Interesting Information).

book_ref.quote: The historic total synthesis of vitamin B₁₂ was achieved by R.B. Woodward and A. Eschenmoser in 1972

blocks.prompt: 71 The total synthesis of vitamin B₁₂ involved:

options.text: over 100 steps, 91 post-doctoral researchers and 12 PhD students

blocks.explanation: The total synthesis of vitamin B₁₂ involved over 100 steps and required 91 post-doctoral researchers and 12 PhD students (Interesting Information).

book_ref.quote: The total synthesis involved over 100 steps and required 91 post-doctoral researchers and 12 PhD students.
